name: The Machines

tenures.source: already World Tag Team Champions entering 1997, retaining against the West Coast Connection at Kickoff '97 (msg_id UBst4BGZDcgJ) and winning the unification match at AEWA Extreme (msg_id TAF-elhQOUQJ)

caption: Held the AEWA World Tag Team Championship into 1997 and became the first AEWA Unified World Tag Team Champions by beating the Assassins in a dedicated unification match at AEWA Extreme.

name: Graphic Violence

tenures.source: already National Tag Team Champions entering 1997 (msg_id huse7tvLE5MJ), lost the title at Kickoff '97

caption: The AEWA National Tag Team Champions entering 1997, dethroned by the Assassins at the fed's own Kickoff '97.

identity.note: The same billing exists in other wings; this entity was minted from its own federation's 1997 documents with no receipt joining it to those — held distinct under the no-auto-merge-and-no-silent-distinctness rule; reopenable on a shared-handler or cross-fed receipt.

name: The Assassins

tenures.source: won the National Tag Team Championship at Kickoff '97 (msg_ids dsrdSnAS4KgJ, KSM5bFgNF_8J), lost the unification match at AEWA Extreme (msg_id TAF-elhQOUQJ)

caption: Won the AEWA National Tag Team Championship at Kickoff '97 and lost that lineage whole two months later, in the match built to merge it into the fed's own new Unified Tag Team belt.

name: The West Coast Connection

tenures.source: challenged the Machines for the World Tag Team Championship at Kickoff '97 (msg_id UBst4BGZDcgJ), champions by 30 August 1997, retaining on 21 September (msg_id zs9AfSi42sUJ)

caption: Challenged for the AEWA World Tag Team Championship at Kickoff '97 and, seven months later, took the fed's own Unified Tag Team belt outright.

name: The NATO Powers

tenures.source: Two-time AEWA World Tag Team Champions, per the fed's own retrospective commentary on the already-served Wednesday Night Rumble (12/11) card: won the inaugural Tag Team title tournament (the fed's own one-year anniversary post, 10 December 1996, already served, credits "the NATO Powers" as its winners), then "beat the Graveyard Shift way back in March" for a second reign, losing it back "2 weeks later." Named as the British Destroyer and the Russian Tank, managed by "NATO" Wally Henderson (Straight Talk 11/15, msg_id 3_8kM9UzGxEJ, already served). Still active as a team as late as Monday Night Live (6/3) (msg_id bgSu_aXLGwgJ, already served), which describes them as having "traded the World Title back and forth in a series of matches that ran from February to April," by which point the title itself is vacant.

caption: A two-time AEWA World Tag Team Championship-winning team from the fed's own opening months, later reduced to an also-ran chasing one more shot.

name: The Graveyard Shift

tenures.source: Billed as "former THREE-TIME AEWA World tag team champions" before winning the belts a fourth time from the West Coast Connection on Wednesday Night Rumble (11/13) (msg_id R2NRybZMF34J), then losing them back to the West Coast Connection ten days later in a tag team triangle match also involving Heaven & Hell, after Vice President Kevin Larkin took over as referee and fast-counted the finish (Saturday Night Slam 11/23, msg_id v588fUUO_iUJ). Named as the Mortician and the Grave Dweller, managed by Coffin.

caption: A four-time AEWA World Tag Team Championship-winning team whose fourth reign lasted ten days, ended by a corrupt guest referee.
